user_turns: I've been thinking about how I am with friendships and something's bugging me.

I love to give people attention for no reason and then move on, I've always been a pretty touchy person, nothing sexual, but I love to hug people, hold their hand, poke them, heck I even give my friends messages (again not sexual) for fun. I definitely give people way more attention than they're willing to give me, which doesn't really bother me, but I've noticed people take me and my attention for granted, as if I'm somewhat disposable.

I'm not socially inept so I can tell people tend to think I'm lesser than them, and they aren't bad people and if you asked them they'd say they don't, but their actions tell another story, like thinking I can't be serious or can't comprehend certain things, which is definitely not the case since, although I'm very private about my merit, I scored in the 1 percentile on the SAT and have kept a very high GPA through college. I get it, I'm an extremely energetic person, but the dilemma is I give people so much attention that they think we're really close friends (or sometimes more), while in reality I don't really care about them that much, I just like giving attention and don't expect much back.

When I move on they get either really angry or really upset, and they clearly have an emotional investment in me since I'm always there to listen to their problems and give solid advice (I was raised by a psychologist who taught me a thing or two about helping people through tough times). During the friendship they always seem to see me as the disposable one, always down to hangout or do whatever, but when I'm ready to move on I feel like they're being disposed of by me, and truthfully I seldom invest in friendships emotionally, I'm quite private, and I'm not sure they're aware I know much more about them than they know about me, so I'm giving them a false sense of friendship.
Am I the Asshole in this situation?

user_turns: So I had my first ever car dealership experience and it didn't go great.

I recently just got my license and started looking at cars I could afford, and since I'd never been to a dealership my dad warned me the salesmen can be very scary and deceiving sometimes and I should always have my "poker face on." I went with my dad and test drove a car in my budget, it drove nicely but I wasn't a fan of the color, and I said so, but the salesman must've thought it wasn't a big deal.

We eventually got sucked into the building and started doing paperwork just to see what he could do for me and how low a price he could get, and after filling out some stuff he got up and went into the back of the building, I'm honestly not too sure where. While he was gone I told my dad we should maybe go look at more cars since I wasn't content with this one yet, he didn't mind and told me to go find the guy and tell him, but I couldn't find him anywhere, I went through all their glass cubicles, so when I walked back to my dad he decided it was okay to leave and look at other dealerships.

After we drove off we started getting several phone calls from the dealership, plus a text from someone else there, not our salesman, basically asking where we went, and I responded "So sorry, looked all over to try to find [salesman], but couldn't find him so we just left to look for other options for now." He texted back how rude we were, that he's never had a customer do that to them and that we wasted their time, and I understand we probably shouldn't have left without saying anything, but I'm not too experienced with car dealerships.
Am I the Asshole in this situation?
